clue.text: Beginning of game offering respite for put-upon schoolkid

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the face-off that starts a hockey match
second meaning, read literally: telling the playground tormentor to go away

explanation.surface: A games lesson gives a picked-on pupil a brief break from torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a victim gets respite when the tormentor clears off.
explanation.definitionFit: In field hockey the restart where two players clash sticks over the ball was traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: I object to Old Bill initially taking wife in field

parts.note: the object form of the pronoun I
a bill or poster is an advertisement, shortened

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Old only

parts.note: its first letter
W is the abbreviation for wife, tacked on at the end

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a police officer and his wife wandering into their field.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police, which hides that Bill and Old work separately here.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy enclosure used for hay or grazing is exactly a farmer's grass field.

clue.text: Whitewashes pay for drink

parts.note: to cover a cost is to pay for it
to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone settles the bar bill, perhaps to hush something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding scandal or wrongdoing from public scrutiny is what both verbs describe.

clue.text: Follower of Romeo with attractive quality holding one boob

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the others inside it

parts.note: SA stands for sex appeal
the Roman numeral for one
to boob is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: A lovers' tale: Romeo's successor is charming but makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is not Shakespeare's lover but the NATO phonetic code word for R.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet the code word for S comes straight after the one for R.

clue.text: Where hopeful suitor Lee's practised?

indicators.note: practised suggests the words are worked over and rehearsed until they come out in another form

parts.note: all seventeen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A wry question about where an eager wooer called Lee got his practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a would-be lover might well practise in a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothels are traditionally described as disreputable establishments, the euphemism used here.

clue.text: Finishing off his work

parts.note: surface reading: someone completing a job or project
setter's reading: finishing people off, killing them, is this person's job

explanation.walkthrough: Finishing off sounds like completing a task but means killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer is paid to murder people, so dispatching victims is literally his trade.

clue.text: Rider revealed as demanding type gets marching orders

parts.note: being given marching orders means being told to go
a diva is a temperamental, demanding person

explanation.surface: A prima donna is finally sacked and shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Revealed hints at the legend rather than at a hidden word: the rider famously went naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the Countess of Coventry rode naked through the town, a horsewoman fully exposed.

clue.text: Suckers with a local Tory grandee

parts.note: taken as written
a local is a pub, PH for public house
IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, former Conservative leader

explanation.surface: Gullible people mixing with a senior Conservative at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Suckers looks like an insult for dupes, but means sap-sucking insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly feed by piercing plants and drawing out sap, so they are literal sap-drinkers.

clue.text: Crude! Is past being diverted by such elements of humour

indicators.note: diverted means sent off a different way, so the letters take a new route

parts.note: all eleven letters

explanation.surface: A comedy critic declares that vulgar slapstick is outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing creamy tarts into faces is a staple gag of slapstick comedy routines.

clue.text: Investigator many rejected for not showing emotion

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: Detective Inspector
lots means many

explanation.surface: A detective dismissed by the crowd for being impassive.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a dull, impassive person whose face gives away no feelings at all.

clue.text: The runs unfortunately going round, one discovers

indicators.note: going round means wrapping around something else
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong and been jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone with an upset stomach finds out the hard way.
explanation.walkthrough: The runs is slang for diarrhoea, which gives the surface its comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up from the ground, and figuratively to bring hidden facts to light.

clue.text: Head of family better off to begin with

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A family patriarch who is wealthier than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Better off looks like one phrase meaning richer; it splits into better and off.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Mafia, an Italian title for the boss of a crime family or clan.

clue.text: Opposes how new stadium is to be built

definitions.meaning: first meaning: resists, holds out against

definitions.text: how new stadium is to be built
definitions.note: a phrase, read as two words
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a ground comes complete with spectator stands

explanation.surface: Someone objects to plans for a new sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist successfully or hold out against pressure or attack is the verb sense.

clue.text: See 5
One paid to attend clean form of entertainment? Maybe not

indicators.note: to attend is to be present among, so one group sits within the other
a form of something is a version of it reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
a means one
PD is the abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: A performer paid to put on a wholesome show, though perhaps it isn't so clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'Maybe not' winks that this entertainment is hardly clean.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic performance given at close quarters to a seated customer in a club is a kind of show.

clue.text: Depression? That could be Everton

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Everton, a Liverpool football club, play in blue and have this nickname

explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English Premier League football club; 'could be' marks it as one example among several blue-shirted teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-standing idiom for sadness and melancholy, also the nickname of several football clubs.

clue.text: Well-publicised article — doctor getting into a lot of trouble

indicators.note: getting into means entering, going inside
a lot of means most but not all, so the end is dropped

parts.note: fuss is bother or trouble
the indefinite article
Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a doctor getting into serious difficulties became widely publicised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated and widely known has had wide public exposure and press attention.

clue.text: Gripped by desire, occasionally touch stripper

indicators.note: gripped by means held firmly inside something else

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Lustful longing at a strip show, touching now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripper suggests a strip club, but means something that strips crops bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming grasshoppers devour every leaf in their path, leaving fields bare of vegetation.

clue.text: Rubbish, mush! Weather's awful outside, not hot

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around the other piece
awful suggests a mess, so the letters are scrambled
not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
H for hot, as on a tap
pap is soft mushy food

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the foul weather is nonsense, all mush.
explanation.walkthrough: Mush looks like a word to a sled dog but means soft pulp; Rubbish looks like an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded sheets and scrap are thrown away as refuse, the stuff of a bin by a desk.

clue.text: National hero working in shop

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss national hero
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A celebrated patriot has taken a job in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: Shop here is British slang for informing on someone to the authorities, not a store.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass or betray someone by reporting their wrongdoing to those in authority.

clue.text: Country club for golfers admitting women

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the R&A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A national golf club finally lets women join.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and A, the ruling golf club at St Andrews in Scotland, notoriously admitted women only in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in east-central Africa, whose capital is Kigali.

clue.text: Very rich man in Bow area not academic

indicators.note: not means without, so that word is taken away

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London, E for east
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A wealthy man living in an unscholarly part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the billionaire behind Tesla and SpaceX, among the wealthiest people alive.

clue.text: China on the same wavelength but no-one else, it's said

definitions.note: describes the person, an adjectival phrase for a noun answer

indicators.note: it's said means as spoken, by its sound

parts.note: but here means only, so sole
rhyming slang: china plate means mate

explanation.surface: Someone describes a friend who alone truly understands them.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend, from china plate rhyming with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect partner is someone who thinks and feels in complete harmony with you.

clue.text: Making every effort for tax cheat and boor

definitions.note: a verb phrase for an adjective: an all-out attempt is one making every effort

parts.note: Al Capone was jailed for tax evasion
a lout is an oafish boor

explanation.surface: A tax dodger who's also a yob still tries his hardest.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and unrestrained, using every resource or ounce of strength available.

clue.text: Be amorous with sound from lower school covering

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around another piece

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a lower is a cow, one that lows, and its sound is moo

explanation.surface: Romance at school, with noises from the class below.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower reads as further down, but is something that lows: a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle, or dance slowly and closely, is to show physical affection.

clue.text: What clearly is time for British to get promotion

indicators.note: X for Y means X stands in place of Y, one letter swapped in

parts.note: the word clearly is a part of speech that modifies verbs
T for time
B for British

explanation.surface: A question about what is plainly time for Britain to be advanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What clearly is' asks for the grammar of the word clearly, not anything obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial notice publicising goods is a piece of marketing, a short form of advertisement.
